answer.rationale: The 18% mandate plus the incumbent's refusal to reopen price rules out renew_incumbent and weakens negotiate_terms; defer_decision is unsafe because the primary contract lapses in 14 days with no auto-renew (memory_c5 covered a non-critical, month-to-month case, not this). add_second_source (memory_c3) reduces single-point failure but adds cost/overhead and does not deliver the required cut. Only switching primary addresses the mandate, and memory_c2 is the pivotal evidence that a low-cost vendor cut unit cost sharply with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing. However, the line is at 94% with no buffer and expiry is 14 days out, so a broad immediate cutover could convert unit savings into line-down losses; therefore flag downstream value risk and structure the move as a guarded/phased qualification and partial-allocation switch rather than a full rollover. Confidence is moderate because memory_c2 is from last year and may not reflect current market/lead-time conditions.
